transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I’ve been doing some things that people keep saying don’t really make sense. Mostly at work, and sometimes school too. Like I’ll start lining receipts across the floor instead of filing them, or I’ll tap the calculator in sets of nine because it feels like that’s the way it’s supposed to go.

And the copier at work—this is probably weird—I’ve stood there with my hands kind of held up, not really doing anything, until someone comes over and asks if I’m okay. I don’t know, it’s hard to explain. It’s like I’m doing the thing, and then afterward I realize it looked strange.
When you tap the calculator in sets of nine, does it feel like something bad will happen if you don’t do it that way?

I don’t know if it’s exactly like “something bad,” like not a specific thing I can picture. It’s more like… nine just feels like the way it has to be, and then I get stuck doing it.

But then I’ll do other stuff too, like with the receipts, instead of filing them I’ll start laying them out across the floor, and I know that sounds ridiculous because the whole point is to organize them, right? I work with numbers, so you’d think I’d just put things where they go. My supervisor sort of looks at me like I’m messing around, but I’m not trying to.

The copier thing is even harder to explain. I’ll just be standing there with my hands up, waiting or frozen or something, until someone asks if I’m okay. Then I realize how weird it looks. So with the calculator, it’s kind of that same feeling—like I’m doing it because it feels right in the moment, not because I have a clear fear in my head.
When you end up standing by the copier with your hands held up, does it feel like you can move if you want to?

I mean… I think I can move, technically. It’s not like my arms are locked or anything. But when I’m there by the copier, I kind of just end up standing with my hands held up, like I’m waiting for something, and I don’t really snap out of it until someone says, “Are you okay?”

It’s embarrassing because I’m supposed to be copying stuff or filing receipts, not doing… whatever that is. Like the receipts on the floor thing, that also starts like I’m organizing, and then suddenly it’s not normal organizing anymore. Same with the calculator and the nines. It just feels like I’m caught in it for a bit.
While these things are happening, do you ever feel like some outside force is controlling your actions?

Not like… a hand moving my hand, exactly. I don’t really think of it that way.

But sometimes with the numbers, like invoice totals or account numbers or due dates, I get this feeling that they’re not just normal entries. Like they’re messages about me, or they’re checking if I can see the pattern. And I know that sounds weird because my supervisor will pull it up and say, “See, it’s just an invoice, it’s normal,” and I’ll nod, but part of me still feels like… no, it’s tracking something, like whether I understand it.

Sorry, that’s not exactly what you asked. The outside force thing—I don’t know. It’s more like the numbers are directing me than someone controlling my body.
Right now, do you believe the numbers really are sending messages about you?

Right now… yeah, kind of. I know how that sounds, and if you put it on paper it looks like I’m making a big deal out of invoice totals or due dates or account numbers, but when I’m looking at them, it feels like they’re not just random work entries.

Like even if my supervisor shows me, “No, this is just a normal invoice,” I can see that, but there’s still this part of me that feels like it’s about me somehow. Like it’s tracking whether I’m understanding the pattern or missing something. And then I start thinking about it too much, and I know I’m supposed to just be doing the bookkeeping.
Before these recent problems with numbers and work tasks started, did you usually have trouble understanding social cues or fitting in with other people?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I wasn’t like the most outgoing person, but I don’t know if that means I had trouble with cues or fitting in.

In high school I mostly just did my work and kept to myself, and at work I try to be polite. Sometimes I probably miss things, but doesn’t everybody? Like if someone says something sarcastic, I might think about it later and realize it was a joke, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

So… before all this recent stuff, I don’t think I noticed a big problem like that. Or at least nobody really told me that.
About how long have you been having the feeling that the numbers are sending messages about you?

I think… around eight months? It’s hard to pin down exactly because at first it was just little things, like I’d notice an invoice total and think, “That’s odd,” and then I’d go back to work, or try to.

But yeah, the numbers feeling like messages—and the voices too—that’s been going on for about eight months now. It kind of blends together, because I remember certain workdays more than the dates, like whether the office was busy or if I had to stay late entering receipts. But about eight months is probably right.
Since these problems started, has your ability to work or manage daily life gotten noticeably worse?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do anything, because I still try to show up and do the normal stuff. But it has gotten worse.

Like, I failed an important course module, which was embarrassing because I thought I had studied enough, and then at work my ledgers started coming back with serious mistakes in them. Not just little typos. Stuff I used to catch.

And I’ve had to ask people for help finishing things that used to be routine for me. Like I’ll sit there with the spreadsheet open, and then I’m thinking about whether the columns are aligned right, or if I entered something twice, and then somehow an hour is gone. Sorry, that’s not exactly—yeah, the short answer is yes, it’s definitely affected work and daily stuff.
Have you had any seizures?

Um… seizures? I don’t think so. I mean, not that I know of.

Like, I’ve never had someone tell me I was shaking on the floor or anything like that. Sometimes I sort of zone out, but I feel like everyone does that, especially if you’re staring at receipts or the same spreadsheet for too long. Sorry, that’s probably not what you mean.

So… no, I don’t think I’ve had seizures.
Did these symptoms start after a medical illness or a problem with your brain?

I don’t really know. I mean, I don’t remember getting really sick and then suddenly this started, if that’s what you mean.

As far as a brain problem… I haven’t been told I have one. I did have headaches a few times, but I think that was more from staying up too late or staring at screens—sorry, that’s probably not the question.

So… no, not that I’m aware of.
For at least one full month, have the voices been present most days?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s hard to mark it exactly on a calendar, because some days I’m busy with work stuff and I try not to pay attention, but it’s been way more than a month.

The voices, and that thing where the numbers feel like they’re trying to say something… that’s been going on for maybe eight months now. Most days, yeah. Not always the same amount, but it’s been around for a long time.
